definition: The task of labeling each word in a sentence with its grammatical role, such as noun, verb, or adjective.
details: POS tagging was a foundational preprocessing step in classical NLP pipelines, though modern deep learning models often learn such syntactic information implicitly without requiring an explicit separate tagging step.

explainer.lead: Part-of-speech tagging labels each word in a sentence with its grammatical role, such as noun, verb or adjective. It was a foundational preprocessing step in classical NLP and still supplies syntax that downstream tasks rely on.

tiers.eli5: It is putting a grammar label on every word, like marking which ones are naming words and which are action words.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers once ran a tagger as an explicit pipeline stage before parsing or extraction. Modern deep models often learn this syntactic information implicitly, so a separate tagging step may add latency without benefit.
tiers.paperLevel: The task assigns each token a grammatical category such as noun, verb or adjective. Its classical role is as a preprocessing stage in NLP pipelines, while deep learning models frequently capture the same syntax without an explicit tagging step.

explainer.example: In a short sentence the tagger marks the article, then the noun, then the verb, giving each word its grammatical role.
